name: mnemon
description: Cross-tool long-term memory backed by mnemon. Recall before answering anything that depends on past decisions, preferences, or project context, and store durable facts the user will expect you to remember. Triggers include "记不记得 / 之前 / 上次 / 我们说过 / do you remember / we discussed".
always-inject: true

# mnemon

mnemon is the source of truth. Alma's own `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` notes are a
per-session log, not the long-term store; durable facts belong in mnemon.

## Use the shim, not the raw CLI

`~/.config/alma/mnemon-bridge/mem` is the only supported entry point. It pins the
store, keeps reads read-only, resolves short ids, and owns the `MEMORY.md` block.
Call it with Bash:

```bash
MEM=~/.config/alma/mnemon-bridge/mem

$MEM find "<query>" [--limit 5] [--chars 240] [--cat preference|decision|fact|insight|context]
$MEM save "<content>" --cat decision --imp 4 [--tags a,b] [--entities X,Y] [--source user|agent]
$MEM show <id-prefix>
$MEM related <id-prefix> [--edge causal|entity|semantic|supersedes|temporal]
$MEM recent [N]
$MEM status
```

Calling `mnemon` directly is only correct when the shim is missing. The raw CLI
needs a full UUID for `show`/`related`/`forget`, does not share the shim's store
pinning, and its `recall --cat` flag is accepted but ignored in 0.2.13.

## Recall

Do **not** query on every turn. A recall costs 0.3–1.2 s and most turns do not
need one. Recall when:

- the user asks "记不记得 / 之前 / 上次 / 我们说过 / do you remember"
- the topic switches to a specific project, service, repo, or host
- the user names something you do not recognise but that clearly comes from
  their history
- you are about to make a decision that may already have been made

Skip it for greetings, small talk, self-contained code questions, and any turn
where the user already supplied the context.

Use the result silently. Do not narrate "I checked my memory".

## Remember

Store one claim per entry, self-contained enough to make sense months later
(with dates, file names, numbers). A conversation usually yields 0–3 durable
entries; store nothing rather than padding the store.

| kind | example | `--cat` | `--imp` |
|---|---|---|---|
| user preference | wording, taste, working style | `preference` | 4 |
| decided course | "use A not B, because …" | `decision` | 3–5 |
| durable technical fact | root cause, config shape, measured number | `insight` / `fact` | 3–4 |
| project background | what a module currently is | `context` | 3 |

`--cat` is mandatory and `general` is rejected: it is the default that turns into
noise. Reserve `--imp 5` for facts that should be visible in every session.

Never store secrets, tokens, passwords, or transient state that a command can
recompute.

## MEMORY.md ownership

Alma injects `~/.config/alma/MEMORY.md` into the system prompt on every request,
and Alma's own instructions tell the model to write to that same file. mnemon
therefore owns exactly one region of it:

```text
<!-- mnemon:begin -->
...
<!-- mnemon:end -->
```

Never write outside those markers, and never edit inside them by hand — use
`mem save` and let `prime.sh` regenerate the block. Everything outside the
markers belongs to Alma and the user.

Keep the block small. It is re-sent on every single turn; treat anything past a
few KB as a permanent cost.

## Guardrails

- Categories: `preference` · `decision` · `insight` · `fact` · `context`
- Edge types: `temporal` · `semantic` · `causal` · `entity` · `supersedes`
- Max 8,000 chars per insight.
- No cross-store queries; `--store "a,b"` is rejected. Query twice and merge.
- Do not create new stores to separate topics.

---
name: mnemon
description: Persistent memory CLI for LLM agents. Store facts, recall past knowledge, link related memories, manage lifecycle.
---

# mnemon

## Workflow

1. **Remember**: `mnemon remember "<fact>" --cat <cat> --imp <1-5> --entities "e1,e2" --source agent`
   - Only exact content repeats are skipped; distinct content is stored and diff suggestions are advisory.
   - To retire a superseded memory, store and verify the new fact, then explicitly run `mnemon forget <old-id>`.
   - Output includes `action` (added/skipped), `semantic_candidates`, `causal_candidates`.
2. **Link** (evaluate candidates from step 1 — use judgment, not mechanical rules):
   - Review `causal_candidates`: does a genuine cause-effect relationship exist? `causal_signal` is regex-based and prone to false positives — only link if the memories are truly causally related.
   - Review `semantic_candidates`: are these memories meaningfully related? High `similarity` alone is not sufficient — skip candidates that share keywords but discuss unrelated topics.
   - Syntax: `mnemon link <id> <candidate> --type <causal|semantic> --weight <0-1> [--meta '<json>']`
3. **Recall**: `mnemon recall "<query>" --limit 10`

## Recall Intent

Keep focused queries and memories in their original language. When the user's
meaning is clear, choose `--intent WHY` (reasons), `--intent WHEN` (timing),
`--intent ENTITY` (what/who), or `--intent GENERAL` (neutral retrieval).
For example: `mnemon recall "<query>" --intent WHY`. The override works in any
language; `--verbose` reports
`meta.intent` and `meta.intent_source` (`auto` or `override`).

Automatic cues cover some forms in English, Mandarin Chinese (simplified and
traditional), Hindi (Devanagari), Spanish, Modern Standard Arabic, French,
Bengali (Bengali script), Portuguese, Indonesian (Latin script), Russian
(Cyrillic), and German. Unrecognized forms use GENERAL; conflicting cues involving
additional languages also use GENERAL. English/Chinese-only scoring is preserved.
This is a lexical heuristic, not full language understanding. See
[the supported forms, script variants, and limits](https://github.com/mnemon-dev/mnemon/blob/master/docs/USAGE.md#recall-intent-detection).

## Commands

```bash
mnemon remember "<fact>" --cat <cat> --imp <1-5> --entities "e1,e2" --source agent
mnemon link <id1> <id2> --type <type> --weight <0-1> [--meta '<json>']
mnemon recall "<query>" --limit 10
mnemon search "<query>" --limit 10
mnemon import --dry-run <file>
mnemon import <file>
mnemon forget <id>
mnemon related <id> --edge causal
mnemon gc --threshold 0.4
mnemon gc --keep <id>
mnemon status
mnemon log
mnemon store list
mnemon store create <name>
mnemon store set <name>
mnemon store remove <name>
```

## Import Historical Chats

When the user asks to import old chats, notes, or exported context, create a
`memory_draft.json` with `schema_version: "1"`, `insights` entries containing
`content`, `category`, `importance`, `tags`, `entities`, and optional
`created_at`, plus optional `edges` using `source_index`, `target_index`,
`edge_type`, `weight`, and `reason`. Run `mnemon import --dry-run <file>`,
then run `mnemon import <file>` only after validation passes. After import,
verify with `mnemon status` and a focused `mnemon search` or `mnemon recall`.
Check the output `errors` field because imports can partially succeed.

## Guardrails

- Main conversation: never run `remember` or `link` directly; delegate to a Task sub-agent.
- Memory sub-agent: you are the leaf writer. Run `mnemon remember` and any justified `mnemon link` commands directly; do not spawn another sub-agent.
- Do not store secrets, passwords, or tokens.
- Categories: `preference` · `decision` · `insight` · `fact` · `context`
- Edge types: `temporal` · `semantic` · `causal` · `entity`
- Max 8,000 chars per insight.

# /add-mnemon

Add [mnemon](https://github.com/mnemon-dev/mnemon) persistent memory to your NanoClaw installation. After running this skill, every agent session will have access to a per-group memory graph that persists across conversations.

## Architecture

# mnemon

## Install & Configure

### 1. Install the binary

**npm** (macOS / Linux / Windows, Node.js 22+):

```bash
npm install --global @mnemon-dev/mnemon
```

Upgrade an npm-managed installation with:

```bash
mnemon update
```

### 2. Set up OpenClaw integration

```bash
mnemon setup --target openclaw --yes
```

This single command deploys all components:
- **Skill** → `~/.openclaw/skills/mnemon/SKILL.md`
- **Hook** → `~/.openclaw/hooks/mnemon-prime/` (agent:bootstrap — injects behavioral guide)
- **Plugin** → `~/.openclaw/extensions/mnemon/` (remind, nudge, compact hooks)
- **Prompts** → `~/.mnemon/prompt/` (guide.md, skill.md)

Restart the OpenClaw gateway to activate.

### 3. Customize (optional)

Edit `~/.mnemon/prompt/guide.md` to tune recall/remember behavior.

Plugin hooks are configured in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "mnemon": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "remind": true,
          "nudge": true,
          "compact": false
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

| Hook | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `remind` | on | Recall relevant memories + remind agent on each message |
| `nudge` | on | Suggest remember sub-agent after each reply |
| `compact` | off | Save key insights before context compaction |

### 4. Uninstall

```bash
mnemon setup --eject --target openclaw --yes
```

## Workflow

1. **Remember**: `mnemon remember "<fact>" --cat <cat> --imp <1-5> --entities "e1,e2" --source agent`
   - Only exact content repeats are skipped; distinct content is stored and diff suggestions are advisory.
   - To retire a superseded memory, store and verify the new fact, then explicitly run `mnemon forget <old-id>`.
   - Output includes `action` (added/skipped), `semantic_candidates`, `causal_candidates`.
2. **Link** (evaluate candidates from step 1 — use judgment, not mechanical rules):
   - Review `causal_candidates`: does a genuine cause-effect relationship exist? `causal_signal` is regex-based and prone to false positives — only link if the memories are truly causally related.
   - Review `semantic_candidates`: are these memories meaningfully related? High `similarity` alone is not sufficient — skip candidates that share keywords but discuss unrelated topics.
   - Syntax: `mnemon link <id> <candidate> --type <causal|semantic> --weight <0-1> [--meta '<json>']`
3. **Recall**: `mnemon recall "<query>" --limit 10`

## Recall Intent

Keep focused queries and memories in their original language. When the user's
meaning is clear, choose `--intent WHY` (reasons), `--intent WHEN` (timing),
`--intent ENTITY` (what/who), or `--intent GENERAL` (neutral retrieval).
For example: `mnemon recall "<query>" --intent WHY`. The override works in any
language; `--verbose` reports
`meta.intent` and `meta.intent_source` (`auto` or `override`).

Automatic cues cover some forms in English, Mandarin Chinese (simplified and
traditional), Hindi (Devanagari), Spanish, Modern Standard Arabic, French,
Bengali (Bengali script), Portuguese, Indonesian (Latin script), Russian
(Cyrillic), and German. Unrecognized forms use GENERAL; conflicting cues involving
additional languages also use GENERAL. English/Chinese-only scoring is preserved.
This is a lexical heuristic, not full language understanding. See
[the supported forms, script variants, and limits](https://github.com/mnemon-dev/mnemon/blob/master/docs/USAGE.md#recall-intent-detection).

## Commands

```bash
mnemon remember "<fact>" --cat <cat> --imp <1-5> --entities "e1,e2" --source agent
mnemon link <id1> <id2> --type <type> --weight <0-1> [--meta '<json>']
mnemon recall "<query>" --limit 10
mnemon search "<query>" --limit 10
mnemon import --dry-run <file>
mnemon import <file>
mnemon forget <id>
mnemon related <id> --edge causal
mnemon gc --threshold 0.4
mnemon gc --keep <id>
mnemon status
mnemon log
mnemon store list
mnemon store create <name>
mnemon store set <name>
mnemon store remove <name>
```

## Import Historical Chats

When the user asks to import old chats, notes, or exported context, create a
`memory_draft.json` with `schema_version: "1"`, `insights` entries containing
`content`, `category`, `importance`, `tags`, `entities`, and optional
`created_at`, plus optional `edges` using `source_index`, `target_index`,
`edge_type`, `weight`, and `reason`. Run `mnemon import --dry-run <file>`,
then run `mnemon import <file>` only after validation passes. After import,
verify with `mnemon status` and a focused `mnemon search` or `mnemon recall`.
Check the output `errors` field because imports can partially succeed.

## Guardrails

- Use the `exec` tool to run mnemon commands.
- Do not store secrets, passwords, or tokens.
- Categories: `preference` · `decision` · `insight` · `fact` · `context`
- Edge types: `temporal` · `semantic` · `causal` · `entity`
- Max 8,000 chars per insight.
